adminContracts.title: Contracts
adminContracts.legal: This is not legal advice: templates are a starting point. Have a lawyer review them before using them with clients.
adminContracts.markup: Markup: "# " title, "## " section (numbered), "- " bullet, blank line = paragraph, {{variable}} for values. Tables: "| cell | cell |" and a "|---|---|" line after the header.

timeline.title: Client process
timeline.hint: The recommended order for working with a client, from the first conversation to maintenance. Create each document from here and the system picks the template and the parent contract.

why.nda: Use it before discussing the project if the client will share sensitive information.
why.sow: What you offer: scope, deliverables, timeline and price. The base the client accepts.
why.services: The formal contract with payments, intellectual property and warranty. Signed before work starts.
why.data_processing: If the system handles personal data of the client's users (Law 1581).
why.change_order: Whenever the client asks for something out of scope: records the change, cost and extra time.
why.acceptance: The client confirms everything was received as agreed. Enables the final payment and starts the warranty.
why.sla: Defines support: what it covers, response times and what is billed separately.
why.retainer: Monthly maintenance with included hours, once the warranty ends.

remind.label: Remind the client by email if they have not signed
remind.onHint: An email with the signing link is sent every N days until the client signs (up to 3 reminders). Each email replaces the previous link.
remind.offHint: No reminders will be sent: the client only gets the initial email.

table.fillHint: Type the data in each cell. Enter moves to the next row and, on the last one, adds a new row.

objeto.why: Describe in one sentence what you will deliver to the client. It is the base of the contract: anything outside the purpose can be treated as a change with extra cost.
objeto.example: Design, development and launch of the client's corporate website.

alcance.why: List what the work includes: modules, screens, integrations. It is what the client accepts when signing and your defense if they later ask for things that were not agreed.
alcance.example: 5-page responsive website, contact form, text editing panel and deployment on the client's server.

entregables.why: The concrete products the client will receive (code, designs, access, manuals). Lets both sides know when the work is finished.
entregables.example: Source code, published site and a PDF user manual.

monto.why: Total value of the work. The contract quotes it with the currency and the payment plan; it is the basis for billing and for penalties.

moneda.why: Sets the payment currency and avoids confusion between pesos and dollars when billing.

hitos.why: How and when you get paid: down payment, intermediate payments and final payment, each with its condition. A down payment protects you if the client disappears, and tying payments to deliveries avoids disputes.
hitos.example: 50 % on signing and 50 % on final delivery.

plazo.why: How long you have to deliver, counted from the start date. It sets the deadline for both sides; if the client delays content or answers, the timeline moves.

fecha_inicio.why: When the timeline starts counting. Usually the signing date or the date of the first payment (down payment).

garantia_dias.why: Time after delivery during which you fix bugs at no cost (new changes are not included). It reassures the client and limits your liability over time.

penalidad.why: What the party that breaches the contract pays, usually a percentage of the contract value. It discourages breaches and avoids having to prove the exact damage.

jurisdiccion.why: City whose courts would settle a dispute if there is no agreement. Choose one where you can attend the process without traveling.

rondas_revision.why: How many times the client can request adjustments on a deliverable before extra is charged. Avoids endless revisions.

vigencia_dias.why: How many days your proposal and its price remain valid. After that you can re-quote.

vigencia_meses.why: How many months the agreement lasts from its start.

preaviso_dias.why: Days of notice required from whoever wants to end the contract. Avoids terminations overnight.

contexto.why: The client's situation and need: where the project starts from. Records why the work is being hired.
contexto.example: The client sells in a physical store and wants to start receiving online orders.

objetivos.why: What the client wants to achieve. It helps measure whether the work met its purpose.
objetivos.example: Receive online orders and reduce manual phone handling.

fuera_alcance.why: What the project does NOT include. It is your best protection against "obvious" requests that were not quoted.
fuera_alcance.example: Content writing, advertising campaigns, hosting and domain.

supuestos.why: What the client must do for the timeline to hold: deliver content and access, and reply on time.
supuestos.example: The client will provide texts and images in week one and reply within 3 business days.

pruebas.why: What you verified with the client before delivery. Records that the work was tested.
pruebas.example: Navigation, forms, test payments and display on mobile and desktop.

observaciones.why: Minor pending items or reservations from the client on receipt. If none, write "None".

tipo_aceptacion.why: Full acceptance (everything as agreed) or with reservations (accepts but leaves pending items). It determines whether you can bill the final balance.

saldo_pendiente.why: What is still unpaid after this delivery, usually the last payment. It is put in writing so you can collect it.

cambio_descripcion.why: Exactly what the client requested. It must be clear so there is no dispute over what the change includes.
cambio_descripcion.example: Add a PDF reports module that was not in the original scope.

cambio_costo.why: How much is added to (or subtracted from) the contract value for this change.

cambio_plazo.why: How many extra days the change needs. It moves the delivery date.

finalidades.why: What the personal data will be used for; the law requires telling the data subject, and you may only process it for that.
finalidades.example: Register orders, send confirmations and manage support.

categorias_datos.why: Which personal data the system handles and about whom. It defines the level of care you must take.
categorias_datos.example: Name, email, phone and address of the client's end customers.

subencargados.why: Third parties that touch the data on your behalf (hosting, email, database). The client must know them.

duracion.why: How long you keep the data; when it ends it is returned or deleted.
duracion.example: During the contract and up to 30 days after it ends.

plazo_incidentes.why: In how many hours you notify the client of a leak or unauthorized access. Usually between 24 and 72 hours.

servicios_incluidos.why: Which tasks the monthly fee covers. Anything not listed is billed separately, so requests do not become unlimited.
servicios_incluidos.example: Security updates, weekly backups and bug fixes.

horas_mensuales.why: Work hours included each month. Unused hours usually do not roll over.

tarifa_hora.why: Price of each extra hour when the client exceeds the included hours.

sistema.why: The product or site the support applies to.
sistema.example: Website and admin panel of example.com

canal_soporte.why: Where the client reports problems. Only reports made through this channel are handled.

sla_horario.why: Days and hours you provide support. Outside them, response time does not count.
sla_horario.example: Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

sla_respuesta_horas.why: Maximum time to respond to a critical failure (system down). Responding is not the same as resolving.

sla_resolucion_horas.why: Maximum time to resolve a critical failure. Promise only what you can deliver.

disponibilidad.why: Share of time the system must be running; 99 % means about 7 hours of downtime per month.

credito.why: Discount for the client if you miss the promised time. It is the agreed consequence, not unlimited compensation.
credito.example: 5 % of the monthly fee per breach.

objeto.why: Why the confidential information and documents will be shared. It limits permitted use: it may only be used for that purpose, and any other use breaches the agreement.
objeto.example: Evaluate and quote the development of an order management web platform for the client.

vigencia_meses.why: Months during which the parties must keep confidentiality, counted from signing. Usually between 12 and 36.
How many months the support agreement lasts from its start.

entregables.why: One row for each thing you deliver, with a short description and its status. Avoids disputes about what was delivered.
What the client receives and accepts with this report. It must match what the contract promised.
entregables.example: Published website | Five responsive pages | Delivered

monto.why: What the client pays each month for maintenance.
The new total contract value including this change: the previous value plus the cost of the change.
